entries.name: diagnose-windows-sandbox-acl
entries.description: Use on Windows for unexpected DSH sandbox access denials: workspace writes or listing fail, or an ordinarily readable path cannot be read. One bundled command inspects the path and every ancestor and repairs the ACL problems it proves in that same run. Expected confinement denials need no ACL repair.

tools.name: body_stop
tools.description: Stop all motion immediately and hold the current pose.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create a persisted goal that keeps this session working across automatic continuation rounds. Use it when the direct human request is a long-running objective, even if the user did not say "goal"; not for single-turn work.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.name: ego_camera_calibration
tools.description: Read fixed RGB camera intrinsics and camera_to_reference transforms into the middle head_camera frame (OpenCV x right, y down, z forward; translation in metres) without images or motion. Each camera has pixel K and dimensions. No absolute camera pose is provided.

tools.name: ego_capture_cameras
tools.description: Capture your left, original and right RGB cameras at one sensor timestamp without moving. Saves three JPEG images and a manifest in your workspace and returns their paths, pixel intrinsics K, and fixed camera_to_reference calibration in OpenCV axes, metres, relative to the original head camera. Includes gripper_pose from the same encoder timestamp, with gripper_to_camera transforms for all three views. Works independently of the console camera display mode. No absolute camera poses or synthesized views are provided.

tools.name: ego_explore
tools.description: Turn in place through a full circle to perceive your surroundings. Use it first in a new place or when an object you need is not in ego_state.

timeoutS.description: Maximum seconds to wait for completion (default 120).

tools.name: ego_gripper_pose
tools.description: Read your gripper-link pose relative to your base and all three cameras from current joint encoders, your body model and fixed camera calibration. No motion or image capture. gripper_to_camera maps gripper-local points (x forward, y left, z up) into each OpenCV camera frame (x right, y down, z forward), translations in metres. The gripper frame is the gripper link origin. Includes sensor timestamp, measured lift/reach and gripper_to_base. For a pose synchronized to images, use ego_capture_cameras and its embedded gripper_pose instead of combining separate calls.

tools.name: ego_observe
tools.description: Report what your camera detects right now (categories and distances). Your world model also updates continuously; use ego_state for the accumulated picture.

tools.name: ego_predict
tools.description: Predict the consequences of a skill before doing it. Returns a receipt with a risk score, the issues found (for example a target whose position is too uncertain to grasp reliably), and the planned motion. Skills: "navigate" (needs x, y, optional yaw in radians), "pick" (needs target), "place" (needs on: a surface, an open drawer to put the object into, or a larger bowl to nest a bowl in; optional offset [dx, dy] in metres in the surface frame; or at: [x, y] to put it down on the floor, optional yaw for its final heading in radians), "open" / "close" (needs target: a drawer; the robot pulls or pushes its handle and ends standing back so the inside is in view). Floor-standing objects such as chairs are picked from beside them, carried a few centimetres above the floor in front of the robot, and put down with at; while carrying them the robot needs more room to turn. Objects inside a drawer are only seen while it is open. If the risk is too high or the skill is infeasible, follow the issues (for example move closer and observe, or choose another spot) and predict again. An infeasible receipt lists blockers: entities in the way, whether they can be moved, and parking spots (parkAt) out of the way; clear a movable blocker first (pick it, place it at a parking spot), then predict the original skill again. A receipt can be run once and expires.

target.description: pick: id of the object to grasp; open/close: id of the drawer.

on.description: place: id of the surface, open drawer or larger bowl to put the held object on or in.

offset.description: place: [dx, dy] on the surface, metres.

at.description: place on the floor: [x, y] in metres.

yaw.description: navigate: goal heading; place with at: final heading of the object (radians).

tools.name: ego_query
tools.description: Find perceived objects by category (for example "cup", "table") and/or near another object. Matching uses each object's role (the scene-level reading of what it is) and then its category probabilities, best match first, so a sideboard partly seen and labelled "counter" is still found.

category.description: Object category or role to look for.

near.description: Id of an object whose surroundings to search, for example "e:3".

tools.name: ego_rgb_recording_start
tools.description: Start background recording of ONLY middle head_camera RGB at a simulation-clock FPS, with same-timestamp measured odometry, encoders and calibration. Does not move the robot. Start before issuing navigation with skill_run wait=false; let this recorder sample independently of model/tool latency, then stop after navigation completes. Do not approximate 2 FPS by repeatedly calling ego_capture_cameras. Recording stops at max_frames or fails visibly on missed samples.

max_frames.description: Recording frame bound, default 256; provider bounds apply.

request_key.description: Stable 8–128 character recording-start key; reuse after lost responses.

tools.name: ego_rgb_recording_status
tools.description: Inspect recording status, actual sensor counts, simulation timestamps and errors. Does not command motion.

tools.name: ego_rgb_recording_stop
tools.description: Stop sampling and finalize all queued middle-camera RGB evidence; cancel=true explicitly discards the recording. If status is finalizing, query status until terminal. Does not stop or start robot motion.

cancel.description: Default false: preserve evidence. True cancels recording.

tools.name: ego_state
tools.description: Read your current understanding of the world: your own position, what you are holding, the skill in progress, and every object you have perceived with its estimated position, position uncertainty in metres, size, what it rests on, and when you last saw it. Objects you have not seen are absent, and positions are estimates.

tools.name: exit_plan_mode
tools.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: Read the current session goal, including the id and revision that update_goal requires.

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Ask a subagent to stop its current work. This call returns without waiting for it to stop. You can continue a local direct child's conversation later with send_message. External executions stop permanently and cannot receive follow-ups. Subagents it started will keep running.

agent_id.description: The id of an agent created under you: your direct child or a deeper descendant.

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List subagents you started, with their ids, labels, and status. running means it is working; inactive means it is not currently working. You will be notified when a subagent finishes; there is no need to keep checking its status. Use send_message to continue the conversation.

scope.description: children (default) lists direct children, which accept send_message in any status. descendants lists the whole tree below you with each entry's parent session id and depth; entries deeper than 1 accept only interrupt_agent.

tools.name: report_problem
tools.description: Alert the operator that you hit a situation you cannot resolve by yourself: an unexpected error, a skill that keeps failing, or a task that cannot be done from here. Before calling, review your own tool calls in this turn and diagnose: which prediction or skill failed, the error text, how often it repeated, where you were, and how it relates to blockers, uncertainty, or missing or duplicate objects in the ego state. The operator console shows the report as an alert. Call it once, then stop.

goal.description: What you are trying to achieve.

step.description: The step you were carrying out when you got stuck.

diagnosis.description: The cause you diagnosed from your tool log and the evidence for it.

message.description: What happened, what you tried, and what you need from the operator.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to an agent. A working agent receives it at its next step; an idle agent starts a new turn with it. Returns delivery confirmation, not the agent's answer.

agent_id.description: The agent id of your direct continuable child, or your direct parent when you are a resident continuable child.

message.description: The message to deliver to the agent.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for a skill. Call it before acting on a task that names or clearly matches a skill in the session skill catalog.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: skill_run
tools.description: Execute the plan of a receipt from ego_predict. Waits for the skill to finish unless wait is false. The robot refuses receipts that are infeasible, expired, already used, or above the risk limit.

tools.name: skill_status
tools.description: Read the state of a running or finished skill.

tools.name: subagent
tools.description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool starts an independently managed subagent and immediately returns its id. The runtime notifies you when it finishes. The child reports results with `send_message`; use `send_message` to steer it while running or continue its conversation after it finishes.

cwd.description: Initial child working directory. Relative paths use your current directory; omitted inherits it. Later directory changes in either agent are independent.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The complete, self-contained task for the subagent. It does not share this conversation's context, so include everything it needs.

tools.name: subagent_fork
tools.description: Delegate a task to a subagent that inherits this conversation: a child agent seeded with all completed turns so far (it does not see the current in-flight turn). Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool starts an independently managed subagent and immediately returns its id. The runtime notifies you when it finishes. The child reports results with `send_message`; use `send_message` to steer it while running or continue its conversation after it finishes.

cwd.description: Initial child working directory. Relative paths use your current directory; omitted inherits it. Later directory changes in either agent are independent.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The task for the subagent. It already sees this conversation's completed turns, so build on them freely and state only what is new.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a task list to plan multi-step work and show progress; skip it for trivial single-step tasks. Add one todo per concrete step before you start. While work remains, keep the todos being worked on `in_progress`, several only when work runs in parallel. Mark each todo `completed` as soon as it is done.

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the current goal.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

action.description: edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. complete and blocked are also allowed during an automatic continuation of this goal; blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Required only with action blocked: the concrete condition that persisted across rounds and blocks progress.
